text: Victor Newman is a fictional character from the American CBS soap opera The Young and the Restless, portrayed by Eric Braeden since 1980. Initially created by William J. Bell as a "despicable, contemptible, unfaithful wife abuser" intended to last only eight to twelve weeks and be killed off by his wife, the character was saved after Bell saw Braeden's performance and recognized his "voice, the power, the inner strength," deciding to sign him to a contract. Braeden was initially hesitant to work in a daytime soap opera, believing it was "too confining," but eventually signed a six-month contract and has remained a regular cast member for over 45 years. Victor is widely described as a ruthless villain with a powerful presence and a low-toned voice, yet he is loving and protective toward family and loved ones, as noted by the show's official website and critics. He arrived in Genoa City, Wisconsin for business and eventually built Newman Enterprises into a worldwide conglomerate. Victor's first marriage was to Julia Newman (Meg Bennett), after which he formed a long-term romance with stripper Nikki Reed (Melody Thomas Scott), who became his wife and mother of their children Victoria (Amelia Heinle) and Nicholas Newman (Joshua Morrow). During his marriage to Nikki, he had an affair with Ashley Abbott (Eileen Davidson), leading to Ashley's pregnancy and the birth of their daughter Abby Newman (Melissa Ordway), who was believed to be Brad Carlton's daughter until age five. Victor was briefly married to Hope Wilson (Signy Coleman), with whom he had a son, Adam Newman (Mark Grossman), who grew up unaware of Victor as his father. Victor has a long-standing business rivalry with Jack Abbott (Peter Bergman) and has had other romantic relationships, including one with his former daughter-in-law Sharon Newman (Sharon Case), which was criticized by both actors and the public. Victor and Nikki are recognized as one of daytime television's most prominent couples, with fans dubbing them "Niktor," and their relationship has been described as a "dominant force" in the show, featuring a continuous cycle of marriage, divorce, and reconciliation. The couple's weddings have been covered by mainstream media, and their dynamic has been praised for its enduring appeal and conflict. Victor has been nominated eight times for the Daytime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series, winning in 1998 and being pre-nominated three times; he also won the "Favorite Male Performer in a Daytime Serial" award at the 18th Annual People's Choice Awards in 1992. In 2007, Braeden received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. In January 1999, Braeden's character appeared on The Bold and the Beautiful in a crossover event from January 25 to 28. In 2008, Victor married Sabrina Costelana (Raya Meddine), a marriage that was short-lived after her accidental death. He later reconnected with Ashley, remarried her, and she became pregnant, though the pregnancy ended in miscarriage. Victor and Sharon Newman's relationship began as a father-daughter bond, evolved into a kiss in 2003, and later included a proposed platonic marriage in December 2011, which was annulled shortly after, followed by a genuine romance. Despite the controversy, Sharon described Victor as her "security blanket" and noted the relationship had "daddy issues" elements, which she said most people do not want to watch. The relationship was criticized as incestuous by Sharon, with fans and actors expressing strong negative reactions. In 2009, Victor and Nikki were temporarily removed from the show due to sudden salary cuts during contract negotiations, with Braeden criticizing the process as "cold and hard-nosed" and "insulting," though a new contract was quickly reached, allowing Victor's return on January 15, 2010. Onscreen, Victor left on November 2, 2009, and returned in 2010. In 2012, further contract negotiations sparked speculation about Victor's departure, with reports indicating a two-week absence and an expiring contract in November, but no final departure occurred. The character has been described as complex, with Braeden noting Victor's deep-seated loneliness, his need for love, and his inability to trust relationships, stemming from his childhood. Braeden stated that Victor "doesn't take any shit" and that he is "defensive and always self-protective," and that he enjoys portraying the character more than anything, despite not being like Victor in personality, as he does not use money to manipulate people. Victor met his mother, Cora Miller (Dorothy McGuire), for the first time at age 7, a scene Braeden called a "deeply-felt" turning point in his career. In 2011, Michael Logan of TV Guide criticized Victor for throwing his ex-wife Diane from an ambulance, calling it "pushing it with the fans," and Braeden defended the character by stating he "doesn't give a shit" and "doesn't take any shit." Victor is considered an icon of the soap opera genre, with his performance widely praised as "legendary" and "enthralling," and he was made a spokesperson for Zellers.

The character of Victor Newman, born Christian Miller on March 7, 1947, in Buffalo, New York, was placed in an orphanage at age seven by his mother Cora Miller (Dorothy McGuire); his father was Albert Miller. By adolescence, he left the orphanage and rose to become one of the world's wealthiest tycoons, changing his name to "Victor Christian Newman," with "Victor" meaning "victorious" and "Newman" meaning "new man." In 1970, he married Julia Newman (Meg Bennet) as he built a strong business reputation. In 1980, the couple moved to Genoa City to assist Katherine Chancellor (Jeanne Cooper) with Chancellor Industries; Julia felt neglected and slept with photographer Michael Scott (Nick Benedict), while Victor cheated on her with Eve Howard (Margaret Mason) and later Lorie Brooks (Jaime Lyn Bauer). Julia became pregnant, believed to be Michael's child, and Victor attacked Michael, resulting in Julia losing the child, which was later revealed to be Victor's. Eve later had child Cole Howard (J. Eddie Peck), believed to be Victor's son. Julia and Victor divorced, and Julia left town with Michael, as Victor began a romance with stripper Nikki Reed (Melody Thomas Scott). Victor taught Nikki about society, took over Prentiss Industries, and schemed to regain it by using Lorie to seduce him into marriage, which failed when Lorie stood him up. Victor later tried to return to Nikki, who had married Kevin Bancroft; Nikki became pregnant with Victor's child but was manipulated into marrying Tony DiSalvo to preserve her relationship with Kevin. Nikki gave birth to daughter Victoria Newman (Ashley Nicole Millan). Nikki later became involved with Rick Daros, who nearly killed her, and was saved by Victor. Eve returned with her boyfriend, demanding money for Cole in Victor's will and later working as his assistant, prompting Julia to return to protect Victor. Victor planned to marry Eve but faked his death on their wedding day and instead married Nikki in April 1984. While vacationing, Eve reappeared with Rick, stole money from them, and escaped. Nikki facilitated Victor's reunion with his mother Cora Miller, who died. Despite loving Nikki, Victor began an affair with Ashley Abbott (Brenda Epperson), enraging Nikki, who then slept with Jack Abbott (Peter Bergman), Ashley's brother and Victor's business rival. Ashley became pregnant, and Victor left Nikki, but when Nikki was diagnosed with cancer, Victor returned to her, and Ashley aborted the child. After Nikki recovered, Victor wanted to be with Ashley, who had moved on with her psychiatrist Steven Lassiter (Rod Arrants); Steven later died, and although Ashley wanted Victor back, he returned to Nikki, resulting in the birth of their son Nicholas Newman (Joshua Morrow). Victor and Jack hired Leanna Love (Barbara Crampton) to write a biography on Victor, when in reality Jack wanted it to be a tell-all exposé. Leanna wrote a chapter about Victor's affair with Ashley and Nikki's illness, leading Victor to believe Nikki was behind it. He divorced her and married Leanna to prove to the press he didn't want to be with Ashley; their marriage was invalid because the divorce wasn't finalized. Victor later took over Jack's family company, Jabot Cosmetics, replacing him with Brad Carlton (Don Diamont), causing Jack to spitefully marry Nikki, making their relationship bitter. Victor married Ashley, and years later told Jack he would give him back Jabot Cosmetics if he divorced Nikki. Jack agreed, but due to a legal loophole, he wasn't given full control. Victor had a heart attack during a confrontation with Jack, left him for dead, and recovered. As Jack and Nikki's marriage strained due to Nikki's alcoholism and painkiller addiction, she reconnected with Victor, who had decided to divorce Ashley. Eve returned with her grown son Cole, who romanced Victor's daughter Victoria, unaware he was believed to be Victor's son. Victor left Genoa City and went to Kansas, letting Nikki and the Newman family believe he had died. He met Hope Adams (Signy Coleman) and returned to Genoa City to marry her. While in Kansas, Cole and Victoria eloped, and when Victor revealed their sibling relationship, the marriage was annulled. After Eve's death, it was revealed Cole was never Victor's son; Victoria and Cole remarried. Victor and Hope had a son, Victor Adam Newman Jr. Hope wanted to return to Kansas, and Victor was not interested; he divorced her, and Victor Jr. was raised without knowing Victor was his father. Nikki was engaged to Brad, which upset Victor. On their wedding night, Victor was shot and Nikki returned to him; the mentally unstable Mari Jo Mason (Diana Barton) was revealed as the gunwoman. Victor and Nikki briefly reunited before he returned to Kansas after Hope's new husband, Cliff Wilson, died. In 1997, Victor married Diane Jenkins (Alex Donnelley), Jack's ex-girlfriend. Nikki had Victor have a vasectomy but froze sperm for future use. Nikki later married Joshua Landers (Heath Kizzier), and in 1998, she was shot by Joshua's ex-wife, Veronica Landers (Candice Daly); Victor divorced Diane to marry Nikki on her deathbed, promising to remarry Diane after Nikki's death. When Nikki survived, their second marriage was invalidated because Victor and Diane's divorce was never processed. Victor and Diane had a bitter divorce over months, during which Nikki reunited with Brad, and Jack and Tucker took control of Newman Enterprises. Diane remained in love with Victor and stole his frozen sperm to artificially inseminate herself; unknowingly, Ashley also stole Victor's sperm. Diane gave birth to Christian Victor Newman, but discovered the sperm was Jack's. Ashley received Victor's actual sperm and gave birth to Abby Carlton, whom she passed off as Brad's child. Victor and Nikki later reunited, and in 2002, Maxwell Hollister (Sam Behrens) attempted to destroy Victor using Lorie Brooks, who had been Victor's estranged wife; Max tried to lead a hostile takeover of Julia Newman Martin's design firm, which Victor prevented. Max then used Lorie to keep Victor and Nikki apart, but Lorie failed, and Max left town. Months later, Victor and Nikki remarried in front of their loved ones. Ashley revealed Abby was Victor's daughter due to her cancer diagnosis, and Victor welcomed her. After rescuing Nikki from a carjacker, Victor was diagnosed with temporal lobe epilepsy. Victor and Nikki's marriage strained as he fought to take Jabot Cosmetics from Jack, managed NVP Retreats, and dealt with Nikki's campaign for State Senator, which led to an affair with her campaign manager David Chow. They eventually divorced after six years in 2008. Soon after, Hope died, and Victor's estranged son, now known as Adam Newman (Michael Muhney), came to Genoa City and worked at Newman Enterprises. Victor fell in love with Sabrina Costelana (Raya Meddine), but she died in a car accident with Nikki's devious husband David Chow. Victor traveled to Mexico and nearly died; Ashley found him and they rekindled their romance. They remarried when Ashley became pregnant, but she miscarried when Adam gaslighted her into believing she was still pregnant. Despite Adam stealing Nicholas' daughter Faith and passing her off as Ashley's, she and Victor divorced as he reunited with Nikki. Victor was later shot by Patty Williams (Stacy Haiduk) and needed a heart transplant, receiving Colleen Carlton's (Tammin Sursok) heart. Victor and Nikki went to treatment in Europe, and upon return, Adam's scheme was revealed—he had faked his death. Victor searched for him in Canada, met Meggie McClaine (Sean Young), brought her to Genoa City, and she worked as Nikki's assistant but caused her to relapse into alcoholism. In reality, Meggie tried to stop Victor and Nikki's union to marry Victor for his money. Victor married her but had her arrested soon after; Nikki moved on with Deacon Sharpe (Sean Kanan). Afterward, Victor's children filed a lawsuit against him over a cosmetics line, which they won. Diane (Maura West), who returned to Genoa City, reconnected with Victor and they remarried, but the marriage was annulled shortly after she found Victor sleeping with Nikki and learned of her affair with Tucker McCall (Stephen Nichols) and Jack. Victor then sent Nikki to a rehabilitation center for her alcoholism. Diane was murdered in August 2011, with Victor as a suspect. Nikki actually murdered Diane in self-defense, causing Victor to falsely confess to the murder to protect Nikki. While in jail, Victor married his former daughter-in-law Sharon Newman (Sharon Case) to push Nikki away; when the entire murder plot was revealed, Nikki was not charged and Victor was freed. Victor and Sharon's marriage was annulled, and he reunited with Nikki, but she left him when some of his past schemes involving Victoria's marriage were exposed. To gain control of the cosmetics line Beauty of Nature, Victor slept with Genevieve Atkinson (Genie Francis). When Nikki reunited with Jack, Victor developed a genuine romance with Sharon to spite her. They married a second time, but he disappeared shortly after, and Sharon believed he was abandoning her. She burned their prenuptial agreement and took over Newman Enterprises, while Jack and Tucker bought up its stocks. While away, Victor lost his memory and worked as a dock worker in Los Angeles, demanding better conditions; workers planned to kill him in an explosion, leading Genoa City to believe he had died, but he returned shortly after. Upon return, he annulled his marriage to Sharon and reunited with Nikki, just before Jack announced he was taking over Newman Enterprises, firing all Newman family members and appointing Adam. However, due to his painkiller addiction, Jack gave up control of the company, leaving it to Adam. Victor and Nikki finally remarried in March 2013, just before Nikki was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. At their wedding, an assassin attempted to shoot Victor, but Adam took the bullet and nearly died for his father. As a result, Adam offered Victor the position of co-CEO at Newman, and they began working together. However, their partnership ended several months later when Victor discovered Adam's silent partner had previously taken Newman private again was Jack. Victor feared Adam and Jack had been scheming to take back the company without him. In retaliation, Victor, who now owned Chancellor Industries according to Katherine Chancellor's will, had all major Newman clients sign with Chancellor, making Newman worthless so he could build up Chancellor. Adam signed over his shares in Newman to Victor, who planned to merge Chancellor Industries with Newman. Nikki revealed she had given birth to another son decades earlier before being with Victor, revealed to be Dylan McAvoy (Steve Burton). A subsidiary of the merged conglomerate, Bonaventure Industries, produced an illegal speed drug that Summer Newman (Hunter King) overdosed on. Jack reported Victor to the FDA, and he and his company were put under investigation. Dylan's supposed father and Nikki's former lover Ian Ward (Ray Wise) arrived in town, causing chaos, and Victor tried to get him out of town. It was later revealed Victor had hired a lookalike to his granddaughter Cassie, named Mariah Copeland (Camryn Grimes), to haunt Sharon and learn a supposed secret she had. When the scheme was revealed, Nick and Sharon shunned him, and Nikki decided to move out temporarily, but she and Victor later reunited. Victor and Nikki learned Ian was incapable of fathering children, causing confusion. It was later revealed Paul Williams (Doug Davidson), Nikki's ex-lover and longtime friend, was actually Dylan's father, causing tension in Victor and Nikki's marriage, which continued when Victor went to great lengths to awaken Phyllis (Gina Tognoni) from a coma to find out more about Sharon's supposed secret. Nikki fell off the wagon and began drinking again; she left Victor and refused to take him back. Victor also sold Chancellor Industries back to Jill (Jess Walton), leaving the rest of the Newman family confused about why he gave it up so easily. In 2015, Victor had Jack kidnapped and replaced by a lookalike, revealed to be a Peruvian drug lord named Marco Annicelli, to take over Jabot Cosmetics and merge it with Newman, forming Newman Abbott Enterprises. Meanwhile, Victor and his children discovered Nikki had fallen off the wagon; they convinced her to quit drinking again, and she and Victor reunited. Jack returned to Genoa City just as Victor learned Marco was dangerous; he planned to shoot Marco in the park, but it was actually Jack who he shot, who had finally returned to confront him. Jack fell into a coma while Victor frantically tried to get rid of Marco, who continued to masquerade around town. When Jack awakened, he reluctantly agreed to help Victor get Marco out of town and back into prison, which they succeeded in doing. With the real Jack back in Genoa City, the Newman Abbott merger ended, and both companies returned to separate states. Meanwhile, Adam, who returned to town under the false identity of Gabriel Bingham, teamed up with Ian (who had escaped prison) to create a computer virus, known as the Paragon project, to destroy Newman Enterprises for revenge; Ian made no promise to stop it. On Halloween, during a party at the Newman Enterprises ballroom, Ian caused the building to catch fire, creating a major panic. As a result, Ashley and Billy (Burgess Jenkins) offered to share office space at Jabot with Newman while the building was repaired, but Victor refused to trust them. It was later revealed Billy revived Paragon as an act of revenge against Victor, leading to Jack firing him and Victor filing a lawsuit against Jabot. "Newman has become a daytime television icon during his unparalleled tenure as soap opera's biggest star ... Victor Newman quickly developed into a main character and firmly planted himself into the hearts of millions of fans across the globe."[57] Chris Jancelewicz of The Huffington Post described Victor as "the very definition of daytime TV icon" and noted that, "Even people who have never seen an episode in their lives know his name, his face, and his powerful low voice."[16] In the early 1990s, he was described as a heartthrob.[58] He is credited as one of the soap opera world's leading stars.[59] Jamey Giddens of Zap2it considers Braeden the soap opera's leading male.[60] Tommy Garrett of Highlight Hollywood stated that Braeden "is known in the industry as the biggest daytime leading man of all time".[61] In 1993, Nancy Reichardt of The Los Angeles Times stated: "Victor Newman is one of those characters. When Eric Braeden first came on the show in the role, Victor was a villain, and what a villain! His portrayal proved so dynamic that this 'minor' plot point has been ignored over the years. Today, Braeden is one of the show's leading men. The character has never lost his edge, but his knife-wielding days are long forgotten."[62] In 1997, The Museum of Television and Radio wrote that with the arrival of the character, who was an "enigmatic stranger popular with women", "the show's revived tableau was complete", saying it was an "amazingly seamless transition" and praised William J. Eric Braeden first joined *The Young and the Restless* in 1980 as a baddy in a mini-stint, but stayed on to transform the show, becoming one of daytime television's most recognizable figures. The character of Victor Newman, a ruthless businessman, was introduced in 1997 as an "enigmatic stranger popular with women," and The Museum of Television and Radio praised the introduction as an "amazingly seamless transition," crediting William J. Bell for the character's impact. Over the years, Victor has remained a symbol of power in Genoa City, with critics noting his dynamic and complex nature. Deanna Barnert of MSN Entertainment stated that Braeden's tenure changed the game in Genoa City forever, and his portrayal has been described as compelling, with critics highlighting his ability to balance villainy and vulnerability. In 1997, the character's arrival completed the show's revived tableau. BuddyTV identified the storyline where Victor locked his wife Julia's lover in a bomb shelter as the turning point that made him a villain. Victor has been used as a spokesperson for Zellers, appearing in commercials that aired in November 1998, where he breaks the fourth wall, praises shoppers, and squashes his nose against the camera lens. According to StrategyOnline, the Zellers campaign was the most popular to date and received considerable praise for balancing affordability with strong branding. Victor's long-standing relationship with Nikki Reed has been called "epic" and has received positive reviews, though it has always been troubled by poor timing and miscommunication. Critics have noted Victor's multiple marriages, including to Ashley Abbott in 1990, Hope in 1995, and their third wedding in 2002 and fourth in 2013, with Entertainment Weekly stating that Victor knows who is best for him—Nikki. His rivalry with Jack Abbott has been a soap opera legend, with Allison Waldman of AOL TV noting their shared wives, corporations, and deep-seated hatred. Waldman praised Braeden for making Victor a compelling, dynamic villain with a heart and vulnerability, likening him to a "big jungle cat" who can turn on those he once loved. Victor has earned nicknames such as "The Mustache" and "The Dark Night." When asked about Victor's commercial appeal, Braeden attributed it to his emotional authenticity and life experiences, suggesting viewers sense his empathy. Tommy Garrett of Highlight Hollywood compared Braeden's performance as Victor to his role as John Jacob Astor IV in *Titanic*, calling both equally enthralling. Victor's voice is described as "gravel," and Toby Goldstein of The Orlando Sentinel credited him as a key factor in the show's enduring popularity. Shelley Fralic of the Winnipeg Free Press named Braeden and Susan Lucci as the soap opera genre's biggest icons, calling Victor the "eye of the Genoa City hurricane" and stating that the show would be unthinkable without him, much like *Dallas* without J.R. Ewing or *The Sopranos* without Tony. In 2022, Charlie Mason from Soaps She Knows ranked Victor second on his list of the best 25 characters from *The Young and the Restless*, noting that his mustache has a space at the Smithsonian and that he has a former-wives wing at the American Museum of Natural History rivaling Henry VIII's.
